subject: Repeated trial credit requests / Lumina Systems - activity review
messages:
From: Evan Price <evan@luminasystems.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, accounts-payable@luminasystems.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request - additional evaluation credits

Hi David,

Thanks again for the trial access — the team has been running several noisy ingestion tests and we've burned through the original allotment faster than expected. Would Redwood be able to issue another $5k trial credit for an additional 14-day evaluation? We're evaluating across two product lines and need the extra headroom to complete perf tests.

Attached: usage-report.pdf (summary of API calls).

Happy to provide more context. If this is a policy question, loop whoever you need.

Best,
Evan Price
Director of Data Platform
Lumina Systems

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Price <evan@luminasystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request - additional evaluation credits

Evan —

Thanks for the note and the usage summary. I can start that conversation, but quick heads up: our system flags a pattern for this account that looks like multiple trial top-ups in a short window (recently in Sep and Oct we issued extra credits as well). Before I approve, I need to confirm the evaluation scope and escalate for a policy/fraud check.

Can you confirm:
- Is the evaluation associated with a single company entity (Lumina Systems) and a single bill-to?
- Are multiple teams within Lumina spinning up separate accounts or API keys?
- Any procurement milestones we should know (PO, SOW)?

I'll loop ops for activity logs and fraud checks — please expect an update in 48–72 hours. If you'd prefer to convert to a paid pilot, I can put a discount option on the table to avoid delays.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Lumina - trial activity log and initial analysis

David / team —

I pulled the activity log for Lumina Systems (attached trial-activity-log.csv). Key observations:

- Multiple account creations tied to the lumina.com domain in the last 90 days (4 unique accounts).
- High churn of API keys: keys rolled >5 times in two-week spans.
- Bursts of identical prompt families from different accounts that map to same IP subnet.

Interpretation: Possible legitimate parallel evaluation across separate product teams OR coordinated attempts to refresh trial credits. Recommend the following next steps:

1) Put a temporary hold on auto-approvals for additional trial credits.
2) Request company-level attestation (PO/contract or SOC2) before granting >$1k in credits.
3) If the customer provides a named procurement contact, allow a one-time manual extension after verification.

I'm happy to run a deeper look if you want session-level traces.

Attachments: trial-activity-log.csv

-Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lumina - trial activity log and initial analysis

Team —

Thanks Marissa, good catch. From security/fraud ops perspective I recommend we decline an automatic credit top-up. Rationale:

- Pattern resembles repeat trial requests we've seen in confirmed abuse cases (cross-account churn + same subnet bursts).
- Allowing another $5k credit without contract raises loss exposure.

Proposed response to customer:
- Deny unvetted extra trial credits.
- Offer an alternative: a limited paid pilot (30% discount for first month) or a capped evaluation credit of $1k pending procurement verification (PO or contract).
- If Lumina provides SOC2 or an established procurement contact, we can re-evaluate and escalate to approve larger credits.

If legal or sales want to push a one-off, require a signed MPA and payment instrument on file.

-Rishi
Head of Risk & Fraud | Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Price <evan@luminasystems.com>
Cc: Jul es Carter <jules@luminasystems.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request - additional evaluation credits

Evan —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed the activity. After an internal review (ops + fraud), we can't approve another unrestricted $5k trial credit at this time. There are indicators in the activity logs that require verification before we can extend larger trial balances.

That said, we want to keep the evaluation moving forward. Two near-term options:

- Quick paid pilot: $1,500 for one month with a 30% pilot discount; will give you full capacity and SLA.
- Conditional extension: one-time $1,000 evaluation credit, contingent on:
  - a single company PO or proof of business entity, AND
  - named procurement contact for invoicing.

If you can share either a PO or SOC2 attestation (or both), we can fast-track a larger credit review. I've attached an invoice template for the pilot to speed procurement (lumina-invoice.pdf).

If you'd like, I can coordinate a 15-minute call with Marissa to walk procurement through the required docs.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192
